Auth.challengeHint: Your password is verified. Enter the current code from your authenticator; this challenge expires around {time}.

Auth.recoveryCodeHint: Your password is verified. Enter one unused recovery code to bind a new authenticator to this account.
Auth.recoveryStartBoundary: Continuing immediately consumes this recovery code, disables the old authenticator, and ends old sessions. Closing the page cannot undo it.
Auth.recoveryCodeHelp: Each code works once. Never send one in chat or a support ticket.
Auth.previewRecoveryCodeHint: MOCK recovery code: MTRX-RECOVER-01 (available after each preview reset).

Auth.recoveryConfirmUnknownHint: The confirmation may have completed. Sign in with the newly bound authenticator to verify the final state.

Auth.challengeReauthenticateHint: The security change is complete. Sign in again with your new password and a fresh authenticator code.

MfaPreview.installHint: Use any standard TOTP authenticator. This preview does not connect a real account or third-party service.
MfaPreview.firstEnrollmentBoundary: Real first-time setup requires the current valid user's own session and current-password reauthentication. Forced password change must finish first, and IAM must prove the factor was never connected or was lawfully removed and that a trusted security-notification address exists. Any unknown prerequisite stops the flow; no login session is issued or upgraded early. Email receives security notices and is not an MFA or recovery factor.
MfaPreview.recoveryBoundary: Recovery does not open the console. Sign in again with a fresh code after setup.
MfaPreview.replaceBoundary: Replacement becomes effective only after confirmation and ends affected old login sessions.
MfaPreview.scanHint: Add the account in your authenticator, or enter the demonstration key manually.
MfaPreview.demoSecret: For UI preview only. This is not a real secret and cannot sign in.
MfaPreview.waitForNewCode: Each code is single-use. Wait for a new code if the current one was used or is about to expire.
MfaPreview.invalidCode: Verification could not be completed. Check the input or restart this flow when needed.
MfaPreview.codesOneTime: Recovery codes appear only now. After closing, they cannot be shown again; generate a new batch after reauthentication.
MfaPreview.codesHint: Store the material in a secure offline location. Each item is single-use; the preview count and format are not a promise about the still-unfrozen live contract.
MfaPreview.codesSaved: I have saved these recovery codes securely
MfaPreview.reenrollCompleteHint: The restricted recovery flow is complete. Return to sign-in and use your password with a fresh code.
MfaPreview.recoverHint: Your current password and recovery code prove identity only for restricted authenticator setup.
MfaPreview.recoverRestriction: The current password and recovery code must both verify. The code is case-sensitive and is consumed on success. It opens only this restricted setup context, issues no session, and cannot disable the account MFA requirement. Leaving or losing the context requires another unused code.
MfaPreview.invalidRecoveryCode: Password and recovery-material verification could not be completed. Check the input; a consumed recovery code cannot be reused.
MfaPreview.noRecoveryMaterial: If both the authenticator and all recovery codes are lost, online recovery is unavailable. Installation-controlled recovery is required; an admin button cannot reset it.
MfaPreview.challengeHint: No login session exists yet. Verify the current password, then enter the authenticator code. If the factor was removed, only the password is required.
MfaPreview.demoPasswordOnly: MOCK input: current password {password}. First-time setup has no existing TOTP and must not ask for one.
MfaPreview.demoLoginChallenge: MOCK input: current password {password}, code {code}. A new login session is created only after both checks pass.

stepUp.hint: This proof is bound to this operation, target, and version. It cannot be reused elsewhere.

MfaPreview.mockBoundary: High-fidelity MOCK for reviewing sign-in, setup, and recovery. It does not enable MFA, retain secrets, or write to IAM. Do not enter a real password or code.
MfaPreview.personalHint: Manage the current signed-in user's own authenticator and recovery material, never another user's.
MfaPreview.removeBlocked: Account policy requires MFA; the last authenticator cannot be removed
MfaPreview.bindRequiresVerifiedAddress: Verify a trusted security-notification address before connecting the first authenticator.
MfaPreview.recoverySummary: Restricted reconnection material for a lost authenticator
MfaPreview.reauthenticationRequired: The connect, replacement or removal has taken effect. The live system must end affected old login sessions; the current session is never silently upgraded or reused for further security changes. Sign in normally to authenticate again. This MOCK does not sign you out.
MfaPreview.reauthenticationActionBlocked: This authentication change has taken effect. Sign in normally again before making another security change.
MfaPreview.accountHint: Controls whether regular IAM users in this account must complete MFA. It never deletes authenticators users connected voluntarily.
MfaPreview.accountControlHint: Account rules and personal authenticators are managed separately. This control does not prove that any person has connected a factor.
MfaPreview.requireForUsers: Require regular IAM users to complete MFA at sign-in
MfaPreview.requireForUsersHint: New users enter first-time setup on their next sign-in; users with an authenticator continue using it.
MfaPreview.reauthenticationWarning: After tightening this requirement, existing regular-user sessions—including the operator's—may require immediate reauthentication. Relaxing it never revives old sessions.
MfaPreview.accountReviewHint: Confirm the impact first, then complete one-time verification for this specific change.
MfaPreview.accountScopeValue: Regular IAM users in the current account
MfaPreview.protectedIdentitiesValue: The root identity and identities with an active platform attachment
MfaPreview.sessionEffectTighten: Tightening requires reauthentication without iterating every session row
MfaPreview.sessionEffectRelax: Relaxing never revives a session that is already invalid
MfaPreview.accountReviewBoundary: Reauthentication is bound to this account, target value, and operation. It is not general authorization and cannot bypass the permission check when saving.
MfaPreview.accountSaveScenarioHint: This selection only exercises recovery paths. It is not a backend request field or public contract.
MfaPreview.accountConflictHint: The save was not applied. Reload the current account rule, then edit from the new baseline.
MfaPreview.verificationDiscarded: This proof was discarded and cannot be used for a new rule version
MfaPreview.accountConflictBoundary: The save is not replayed automatically, and the password or verification code just entered is never reused. Reload, review, and verify again.
MfaPreview.accountDeniedTitle: This identity cannot update the account rule
MfaPreview.accountDeniedHint: Reading and updating the rule are separate capabilities. Seeing the current value does not imply permission to change it.
MfaPreview.accountDeniedBoundary: The save was not applied and the visible rule is unchanged. The one-time proof, password and verification code were discarded; nothing is retried automatically.
MfaPreview.accountUnknownTitle: The account-rule save outcome is unknown
MfaPreview.accountUnknownHint: The request may have committed or may not have applied. A network or 5xx response is not definitive failure.
MfaPreview.accountUnknownBoundary: A second save cannot start while the original intent is locked. The password, verification code and operation proof have left the page; only the authoritative result of the original intent may be queried.

accountInspectionErrors.notFound: The original intent has no definitive result yet. It remains unknown and cannot be saved again.
accountInspectionErrors.unavailable: The original intent cannot be queried now. It remains unknown; retry later with the same intent.

MfaPreview.accountInspectionUnavailable: Both the save and the local recovery journal are unavailable, so this MOCK session cannot safely inspect the original intent. Account-rule writes remain closed across ordinary refreshes and route changes; end and re-enter the preview session to reset it. This boundary does not imply that a real platform may replace authoritative result lookup with signing in again.
MfaPreview.accountMockBoundary: This account rule writes only to the isolated preview repository. IAM has not frozen public security-settings HTTP; a real failure must never fall back to this MOCK.

SecurityNotificationPreview.title: Security notifications
SecurityNotificationPreview.hint: Manage the signed-in user's own security-event address. It is not a sign-in name, MFA factor, or recovery credential.
SecurityNotificationPreview.cardHint: Receives notices about authenticator, recovery-code, and account security-setting changes.
SecurityNotificationPreview.firstSliceBoundary: The current design covers only the user's first address. Replacing or removing an existing address requires the current password and target-bound strong proof; this MOCK provides no weaker bypass.
SecurityNotificationPreview.completed: The security notification address is verified only in this page's MOCK state. Nothing was written to IAM and no real email was sent.
SecurityNotificationPreview.flowTitle: Verify the first security notification address
SecurityNotificationPreview.flowHint: Reconfirm the current password, then confirm the 8-digit code sent to the target address.
SecurityNotificationPreview.mockBoundary: Explicit MOCK: this does not connect to SMTP, send email, or store input in browser storage or IAM. Do not enter a real password or private email address.
SecurityNotificationPreview.emailHint: The first slice accepts one ASCII email address. The address is never a sign-in or recovery method.
SecurityNotificationPreview.invalidCredentials: The email format or MOCK password is invalid. No verification intent was created.
SecurityNotificationPreview.flowBoundary: The real service spends persistent send budget before creating an intent and rechecks the current session, password generation, and contact revision at commit.
SecurityNotificationPreview.verifyHint: The code proves current possession of the address only. It cannot sign in, reset a password, remove MFA, or grant permission.
SecurityNotificationPreview.pendingBoundary: Only a page-local verification intent exists and its state is PENDING. This MOCK called no SMTP channel and has no evidence of acceptance, final delivery, or reading.
SecurityNotificationPreview.codeHint: A real code is single-use. Wrong attempts spend the shared budget; a new session or intent does not refund it.
SecurityNotificationPreview.invalidCode: The code is invalid, used, or expired. The address remains unverified.
SecurityNotificationPreview.stateVocabulary: Real delivery distinguishes PENDING, IN_FLIGHT, RETRY_WAIT, ACCEPTED, FAILED, and EXPIRED. It never overwrites an unknown result with “delivered.”

OwnSessions.activeHint: Only login sessions that can still make protected requests for the current user are shown.
OwnSessions.confirmHint: Future protected requests made by this session will be rejected.

OwnSessions.emptyHint: This page has no active login sessions.

OwnSessions.currentAbsent: A later page may omit the current session. That does not mean the current session has signed out.

RoleSelfService.title: Role switch preview
RoleSelfService.mockBoundary: Isolated member MOCK for reviewing role discovery, assumption, and exit. It does not change the signed-in user in the header, issue a real credential, or read the administrator role directory.
RoleSelfService.actorHint: This scenario actor can assume eligible roles but cannot list, edit, or administer roles or sessions.
RoleSelfService.assumeOnly: Can only discover and assume roles that satisfy every condition
RoleSelfService.scenarioHint: Switches MOCK outcomes only, so the recovery UX can be reviewed against the real contract.
RoleSelfService.discoveryHint: Only roles this member can assume now are returned. Unauthorized roles are not disclosed.
RoleSelfService.discoveryBoundary: Eligibility is not role-management authority and does not promise that future business requests will be allowed. Every request is authorized again.

purposes.productionLogs: Temporarily review production logs without role editing or session administration.

RoleSelfService.reviewHint: Confirm the source identity, role, and lifetime before creating a new preview intent.
RoleSelfService.durationHint: Cannot exceed the role limit of {max} minutes. Expiry is only one lifecycle terminal state.
RoleSelfService.unknownOutcome: Safe retry boundary: a real request keeps requestId {id}. If the outcome is unknown, query the original request instead of issuing another. If its credential was lost, revoke the original intent before assuming again.
RoleSelfService.deniedHint: The service returns a generic denial. Do not guess whether trust, assume permission, role state, or a permission boundary changed. Discover currently assumable roles again.
RoleSelfService.conflictHint: A 409 is not specific to a stale role version and does not prove the original requestId was never submitted. This MOCK knows the intent is fresh, never reused, and had no earlier UNKNOWN outcome, so it can rediscover assumable roles for review. An uncertain origin must query the original request first.
RoleSelfService.uncertainHint: Do not submit again. Keep the original requestId ({id}) and query that assumption intent first.
RoleSelfService.locatedTitle: The original request created a session
RoleSelfService.locatedHint: A non-secret session record {id} was found, but the query endpoint never reveals the role credential again.
RoleSelfService.credentialUnavailable: This client cannot use the session. Revoke the confirmed session before creating a new intent safely.
RoleSelfService.revokedHint: A new assumption intent can now use a new requestId without leaving an unknown parallel session.
RoleSelfService.activeHint: This shows the information hierarchy after self-service succeeds. A real role identity must be revalidated from its role credential.
RoleSelfService.noCredential: The preview never displays or stores a real role credential and never replaces the header sign-in. A real first success reveals the secret once; an equal replay does not reveal it again.
RoleSelfService.confirmExitHint: A real logout only terminates the role session. It does not restore or issue source-user credentials; that source session must be checked again.

AccountAccess.enableHint: Enabling allows sign-in with a valid password. Revoked sessions are not restored.
AccountAccess.resetHint: Resetting revokes all current sessions and requires a password change at next sign-in. It does not re-enable a disabled user.
AccountAccess.immutableUserFieldsHint: The user ID, sign-in name and owning account cannot be changed. Profile updates change only the display name.
AccountAccess.liveCredentialContractHint: The live IAM contract does not yet provide console access, programmatic access or credential inventory. This view does not infer access methods from user status.
AccountAccess.deleteUserImpact: Deletion cannot be undone. The sign-in name and user ID remain permanently reserved; passwords, sessions and direct policy attachments are invalidated. Resources, running workloads, operations and audit records owned by the account remain.
AccountAccess.directoryHint: The primary identity owns the account's resources. Subusers have independent identities and access only what is granted.
AccountAccess.primaryProtectedHint: The primary identity owns the account. Subuser management cannot grant it permissions, disable it, reset its password or delete it.
AccountAccess.primaryCredentialsHint: Primary and subuser credentials are managed separately. This page cannot create primary account keys or reset its password. Use subusers for everyday work.
AccountAccess.ownerPermissionsHint: The primary identity has full access to resources owned by its account without subuser policy associations. This does not grant access to other tenants or platform-wide privileges.
AccountAccess.rootIdentityBoundaryHint: The account root identity is not a regular user. It cannot join groups or receive ordinary permission policies. Separate protected capabilities govern account recovery and other root operations.
AccountAccess.subuserOwnershipHint: This subuser belongs to the current account, which also owns resources the subuser creates. Administrator permissions do not make a subuser the primary identity.
AccountAccess.accessPermissionHint: Access methods control how a user signs in or calls APIs, not resource permissions. Access also requires valid credentials, an active identity and appropriate authorization.
AccountAccess.permissionSourceHint: Direct policies and group inheritance are shown separately. Removing a direct association does not remove the same policy inherited from a group. Administrator permissions do not change user type; effective access must evaluate all policies and boundaries.
AccountAccess.noUsersHint: Create subusers and grant permissions as needed.
AccountAccess.userPageHint: Search, filters and select-all cover regular users on this page only. The account owner is shown separately above.
AccountAccess.aliasSubtitle: A dedicated sign-in identifier for the primary account
AccountAccess.aliasHint: Subusers can use this alias instead of the primary account ID to sign in. It is not an email address, domain, or the primary account's username.
AccountAccess.aliasPending: Available after an alias is set
AccountAccess.aliasRule: 3–63 characters, starting with a lowercase letter. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only; no trailing hyphen. Unique across the platform.
AccountAccess.aliasChangeHint: The old alias stops accepting sign-ins and stays reserved for this tenant. Existing sessions and resource ownership are unchanged; account-ID sign-in still works.
AccountAccess.aliasAdminHint: Contact your primary account administrator to configure or change this alias.
AccountAccess.tenantAdminHint: Only the platform bootstrap administrator can create tenants
AccountAccess.tenantScopeHint: Creating a tenant does not grant cross-tenant access
AccountAccess.tenantLifecycleHint: This area manages the account and recovery of its root identity. It does not grant access to account resources or change resource ownership.
AccountAccess.disableTenantHint: Disabling rejects new protected requests and revokes current sessions. It does not delete resources, audit history or already accepted background operations.
AccountAccess.enableTenantHint: Users must sign in again after access is restored. Revoked sessions and policy attachments are not restored automatically.
AccountAccess.recoverRootHint: Set a one-time initial password only for this account's existing root identity and require a change at next sign-in. This does not promote a user or grant platform access.

AccountAccess.defaultDenyHint: Access is denied unless granted. Resources created by subusers belong to the primary account and share its quotas. Tenants cannot access each other by default.

AuthorizationProfilePublishingPreview.title: Product onboarding review · {product}
AuthorizationProfilePublishingPreview.subtitle: An internal engineering workflow prototype from product declaration to trusted registration
AuthorizationProfilePublishingPreview.boundary: This flow previews collaboration between product engineering and IAM. It is not a tenant self-service publishing surface, writes nothing to the IAM registry, and grants no permissions.

declaration.title: Confirm the product-owned permission declaration
declaration.lead: This view reuses the real AuthorizationProfile shape from the catalog. It displays the current declaration read-only and does not recompute its digest in the browser.
declaration.ownerHint: The product team defines Actions, resource kinds, target shapes, and trusted conditions, then ensures real product APIs enforce the same declaration. Registering names alone does not complete product onboarding.

validation.title: Review the IAM contract and real enforcement boundary
validation.lead: A future controlled onboarding flow must prove each item below. This is a UX checklist, not evidence that the browser called an online validation service.

namespace.title: Namespace and version ownership
namespace.hint: Confirm that product, callingService, Action prefixes, and revision are owned by the product team, and that one revision cannot be overwritten with a different digest.

resources.title: Action and resource model alignment
resources.hint: Review resourceKind, authorization target shapes, result resources, and TENANT versus platform scope for every Action.

subjects.title: Subject types and user credential carriers
subjects.hint: Review subjectTypes and userAuthenticationMethods for each Action. USER support does not imply both login sessions and access keys, and ROLE cannot inherit a USER capability implicitly.

conditions.title: Conditions use trusted value sources
conditions.hint: Accept only IAM-declared identity and transaction-time attributes; products and tenants cannot inject arbitrary caller attributes.

enforcement.title: Real PEP enforcement evidence
enforcement.hint: Product APIs must check the matching Action and cover resource ownership, list filtering, and bulk operations instead of relying on catalog registration alone.

validation.notProof: IAM currently exposes code-level pure validation and a read-only directory only. These checklist items are not an online validation result, approval record, or release credential.

release.title: Review the immutable release reference and consumption boundary
release.lead: A trusted release identifies content with an exact product, revision, and contentDigest. Catalog visibility and permission grants remain separate concerns.

boundaries.noGrant: Catalog registration grants no permissions to a user, group, role, or service.
boundaries.immutable: A revision remains immutable; a different digest cannot overwrite an existing revision.
boundaries.noExpansion: A higher revision does not expand existing policies automatically; policies retain their resolved capability snapshot.
boundaries.serviceConsent: Cross-product operations still require a separate service identity and customer consent. Product onboarding does not unlock every tenant resource.

release.unavailable: IAM does not yet provide AuthorizationProfile drafts, online approval, a publish API, or a matching publish Action. Final publishing is always unavailable in this prototype.

ServiceAuthorizationPreview.title: Service authorization
ServiceAuthorizationPreview.subtitle: An isolated MOCK of explicit customer consent for a cloud service to operate resources
ServiceAuthorizationPreview.boundary: Product onboarding, service identity, and customer authorization are separate boundaries. Template IDs, service principals, and role names here are UX examples. This page creates no role, issues no temporary credential, writes nothing to IAM, and does not mean this tenant has granted consent.

directory.title: Service authorization templates available for review
directory.hint: Cloud products and the IAM platform publish templates through a controlled process. Tenant administrators review and consume them; they cannot register platform Actions.
directory.separation: Ordinary service roles remain managed in the role directory. This page previews service-linked-role customer consent; sharing a service principal does not merge the two concepts.

detail.title: Service authorization template
detail.hint: Confirm who represents the service, why access is needed, and the exact policy snapshot permitted after consent.
detail.trustTitle: Trust only the registered service subject
detail.trustHint: A callingService or ordinary service name is not a customer delegation credential. A future flow must still verify workload, purpose, and target account.
detail.permissionHint: Customer consent binds an exact policy version. Catalog or template revisions cannot silently expand an existing grant.
detail.policyNavigationHint: Policy details open the current default v{current}; this service authorization still reviews pinned v{version}. One cannot substitute for the other.
detail.policyUnavailable: The policy v1 pinned by this template is unavailable in the MOCK. The review cannot fall back to the default version or continue.
detail.ordinaryRole: The existing PipelineDeploymentRole is an ordinary workload role, not an existing instance of this service authorization. This page does not rename or reuse it to fabricate customer consent.

template.purpose: Operate application delivery and pipeline tasks on behalf of the tenant

identity.title: Confirm service identity and one purpose
identity.lead: The authorization target is a trusted service subject requesting access to this target account for one stated purpose—not any service in the product catalog and not an ordinary user credential.
identity.passRoleBoundary: A future PassRole or role assumption must jointly verify the actor, target account and role, actual workload, and service purpose. This UX example has no workload proof and does not mean the service can assume the role.

permissions.title: Confirm the immutable permission snapshot
permissions.lead: Review every operation the service could perform for the tenant. A policy name is only navigation; authorization must bind exact content and version.
permissions.crossProduct: This snapshot includes both PaaS and DevOps capabilities. Cross-product operation must be explicit before consent; onboarding a product to IAM does not grant these permissions automatically.

consent.title: Confirm customer consent and revocation boundaries
consent.lead: Only explicit customer consent can create a service-linked role scoped to this account and purpose. This MOCK does not perform that action.

explicit.title: Explicit customer consent
explicit.hint: Catalog visibility, product installation, and service authentication do not replace authorization by this account.

shortTerm.title: Short-lived sessions only
shortTerm.hint: The service would assume a dedicated role for constrained temporary credentials instead of receiving a customer's long-lived key.

noExpansion.title: Template revisions never auto-expand access
noExpansion.hint: A new template or revision requires review; existing consent retains its original permission snapshot.

cleanup.title: Check associated resources before deletion or cleanup
cleanup.hint: Associated resources must block service-linked-role deletion or enter an explicit asynchronous cleanup flow. Backend contracts must still define authorization revocation and when existing short-lived sessions expire.

consent.unavailable: IAM has not published tenant authorize, revoke, or assume-role contracts for ServiceRoleTemplate. Final authorization stays disabled and cannot produce a success state.

UserBoundary.title: Permission boundary (limit only)
UserBoundary.hint: A boundary limits this user's permission ceiling. It grants no permissions and does not change attached policies. It follows the boundary policy's current default version; the backend still authorizes every access.

RoleWorkspace.boundaryChangeHint: Changing or removing a boundary can change effective permissions immediately, including existing preview role sessions. It does not add or detach grant policies.

RoleWorkspace.noPermissions: No policies attached · resource access is denied

RoleWorkspace.invalidMetadata: Check tags and session duration. Use unique tag keys and a duration of 15–720 minutes.
RoleWorkspace.reviewHint: Creating trust does not grant callers permission to assume the role. Account users still need an explicit grant for iam:assumeRole.
RoleWorkspace.cancelHint: The unsaved trust, policies and role details will be discarded. Nothing has been created.
RoleWorkspace.noTrustChanges: No trusted identities have changed. Adjust your selection before reviewing.
RoleWorkspace.trustChangeHint: This trust replaces the previous trusted identities for new sessions. Existing sessions retain their expiry; revoke them separately if needed.
RoleWorkspace.settingsChangeHint: Changes apply to newly created sessions. Existing sessions are not extended or revoked. Console access here is MOCK metadata, not a sign-in action.
RoleWorkspace.policyChangeHint: The selected change affects this role's current and future preview sessions. Caller policies and the boundary are unchanged. Removing one grant does not remove equivalent grants from another policy.
RoleWorkspace.requiredAction: An account user also needs the following action/resource grant. The trust document above is not this grant.

errors.enrollmentStart: First enrollment could not start. Confirm the notification address is verified and the security revision is current.
errors.enrollmentOutcomeUnknown: The enrollment submission outcome is unknown. This page kept the original requestId; query it before doing anything else and do not resubmit.
errors.enrollmentInspect: The original enrollment intent cannot be queried right now. Keep this page and requestId, then try again later.
errors.enrollmentNotFound: IAM cannot find the original request right now, but that does not prove it was never submitted. Keep querying the same requestId and do not create another intent.
errors.enrollmentConfirm: The authenticator code could not be confirmed. Check it; do not create a second intent when the outcome is uncertain.
errors.cancel: The enrollment could not be cancelled. Keep this page open and retry.

AccessSimulator.exampleHint: Fills the request only. No policies or memberships change; results use your current preview data.

path.label: Resource path scope
path.hint: Compare production/payment with archive/payment. Both have production tags, but this user's grant matches only the production/ path.

duplicate.label: Direct and inherited grants
duplicate.hint: Inspect the same policy arriving directly and through a group. Removing just one grant source may leave another applicable source.

tags.label: Resource-tag authorization
tags.hint: This resource has production tags despite its archive/ name. Compare it with a staging topic; policy metadata tags do not control access.

deny.label: Matching explicit deny
deny.hint: Inspect the production deployment guard, then compare a staging deployment. A deny matters only when its action, resource and conditions match.

boundary.label: Permission boundary
boundary.hint: The group grants application operations, but this user's boundary excludes deletion. Compare the same resource's deployment operation.

ungranted.label: Console access without grants
ungranted.hint: The user has console access enabled in MOCK, but no resource grants. Login method and policy permissions are independent.

AccessSimulator.disabledUser: This user is disabled. You may inspect their policies, but this simulation does not validate login or credentials.
AccessSimulator.notEvaluated: Not evaluated: account/user availability, credentials, real sessions and product-side enforcement. A policy allow is not proof that a real request will succeed.
AccessSimulator.sessionScope: This diagnostic also checks the selected MOCK session's expiry, revocation and role/caller existence. It does not validate real STS credentials or inherit the caller's user policies.
AccessSimulator.scope: Simulates current-tenant user grants or a preview role session, intersected with its boundary. No real resources, external identity verification or backend authorization. Cross-account, resource policies and role chaining are unsupported.
AccessSimulator.contextHint: Used for conditions only. Leave blank to test missing-context behavior.
AccessSimulator.evidenceCount: {count} evaluation records, including the current default version and grant source.
AccessSimulator.beforeRun: Choose a user or preview role session, action and test resource, then run the simulation. No real resources will be read or changed.
AccessSimulator.noUsersHint: Create a preview user before checking their policy grants.
AccessSimulator.noGrantsHint: This user has no direct policies or inherited group policies. Access is denied by default.

explanations.allow: Grant policies allow this request, and a configured boundary must also allow it. No matching deny or missing decision context was found. Applies only to this simulation.
explanations.explicitDeny: An explicit deny matched. Other allow statements cannot override it.
explanations.implicitDeny: Grant policies or the configured boundary did not allow this action, resource and context. Inspect the evidence for each source.
explanations.indeterminate: Condition context or a readable policy is missing. This result cannot be treated as permission to access a resource.
explanations.invalidRequest: Check that the user, action and test resource are within the supported simulation scope.

errors.unknownIdentity: This user could not be found. Choose a user in the current tenant.
errors.unknownResource: The test resource is missing or its reference is invalid.
errors.crossTenant: The resource belongs to a different tenant. Cross-tenant access cannot be simulated.
errors.unknownAction: The action is not in the supported Matrix action catalog.
errors.actionResourceMismatch: The selected resource type is not supported by this action.
errors.requiresRoleTrust: Assuming a role also requires trust-policy and session checks. A user-policy simulation cannot determine this.
errors.expiredSession: The session has expired. Changing request time cannot extend its lifetime.
errors.revokedSession: This preview session has been revoked.
errors.unavailableSession: The session, role or original caller is unavailable.

AccessSimulator.boundaryResult: Boundary {name}: {decision}. Grant policies must also allow the request.
